Confirmed at published p. 76, printed as quoted: 'To a section s ∈ B, we associate the surface T := {rv² = sw²} ⊂ X with projection p : T → S. It is a finite double cover of S ramified over Δ.' It is not finite. Over a point x ∈ S the fibre equation is r(x)v² − s(x)w² = 0 on the fibre P¹ of X = P_S(O_S ⊕ L); this is a nonzero binary quadric, hence cuts out a finite scheme, unless r(x) = s(x) = 0, in which case it vanishes identically and the whole P¹ lies in T. Since D = {s = 0} meets R = {r = 0} (B consists of sections whose zero locus meets R transversally in its smooth locus), that locus R ∩ D is non-empty in general. The paper itself confirms the correction one page later: on p. 77 it defines 'S⁰ := S ∖ Sing(Δ) the locus over which p is finite flat', and Sing(Δ) = Sing(R) ⊔ (R ∩ D). Over Sing(R) the map is still finite — there r = 0 but s is a unit, so the fibre equation is w² = 0, the ordinary double point the paper describes. So the non-finiteness is exactly over R ∩ D. The classification 'affects a stated result' is right for the sentence itself, while nothing downstream breaks, because §3.2 onwards works over S* and S⁰ throughout. Confirmed at published p. 87, given the normalisation fixed on p. 86. Section 5.1 chooses the component of the strict transform 'where v = √a₁ g w', so on C the trace-zero root is z = rv/w = √a₁ rg. The map in (5.5), 0 → p_*O_T(−C) → O_S ⊕ L^{⊗−1}(−R) → O_C, is therefore (1, √a₁ rg), while the paper prints (1, rg); the same coefficient recurs in (5.6) on p. 88. Harmless, and the extraction says why: s was chosen with a₁ > 0, so √a₁ is a non-zero real scalar and may be absorbed by renormalising g, and the later step only needs injectivity of cup-product with ∂(rg), which a non-zero scalar does not affect. No later version or erratum corrects it: arXiv 1804.03642 stops at v2, Crossref's record of doi:10.1007/s10240-019-00108-7 carries no update-to, updated-by or relation entry, and the IHES volume lists no corrigendum (checked 23 September 2026). sourceIssues.locator: Published Lemma 6.4, p.92; arXiv v2 p.24; author PDF p.30
sourceIssues.printed: The source claims the choice t := −h1h2ru succeeds.
sourceIssues.correction: Choose h1 with real divisor H−R: a simple pole on R and simple zero on H. Clear its other polar divisor D away from the real locus with the stated sum of squares, then t=−h1h2ru has the required real divisor H.
sourceIssues.reason: The printed choice gives h1 a simple zero on R. With u a section of A^lN²(−2R), multiplication by r to reach A^lN²(−R) leaves order_R(h1)+order_R(r)=2 in the target-line trivialization. Thus t has an unwanted double zero on R and cannot have the asserted smooth real zero locus. Reversing that real divisor coefficient gives −1+1=0 and preserves the prescribed sign argument; item 83 records the repair.
